key_insight: DeltaBox reduces checkpoint/rollback (C/R) latency from hundreds of milliseconds or seconds to the millisecond range by storing and applying only the incremental changes to a sandboxed agent state rather than duplicating the entire state each time.
problem_solved: High-frequency state exploration for LLM-powered agents (e.g., test-time tree search, RL) is bottlenecked by slow full-state checkpoint/rollback, limiting search depth, parallelism, and throughput.
method: Incremental/delta checkpointing: capture only page- or object-level differences between successive checkpoints to avoid full-state duplication.
Copy-on-write and overlayed sandboxing: use overlays for files and memory to materialize changes lazily and enable instant metadata swaps for rollback.
Lightweight process-state capture and replay: track and restore essential runtime context (memory pages, open descriptors, interpreter state) with minimal serialization overhead.
impact: By cutting C/R latency to milliseconds, DeltaBox enables much deeper and wider state exploration, dramatically increasing search throughput and scalability for stateful LLM agents in RL, planning, and concurrent fan-out use cases.
visual_elements: Latency bar chart: 'Full duplication' vs 'DeltaBox' showing ms vs 100s ms–s C/R times.
Architecture diagram: sandbox layers (file overlay, memory diffs, process context) and fast rollback flow.
Sequence diagram: repeated checkpointing during tree search showing small deltas accumulating and fast rollback to prior nodes.
Scalability heatmap: number of parallel rollbacks / search breadth enabled at different C/R latency values.
paper_title: DeltaBox: Scaling Stateful AI Agents with Millisecond-Level Sandbox Checkpoint/Rollback
paper_authors: Yunpeng Dong, Jingkai He, Yuze Hou, Dong Du, Zhonghu Xu
